title: Choose the visual world for the ACCS design system
question: The roll assigned Office Hours. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Office Hours
options.lineage: the weekly consultation timetable taped to a CCS faculty door
options.thesis: Every screen is a ruled week sheet: content arrives as timetable blocks, and the restricted lane is drawn into the grid, not hidden.
options.viewport: Door plate and headline on the left; this week's ruled grid on the right with community, consultation and a hatched reports lane, a live now-line crossing today.
options.risk: Reads as a calendar clone if every component turns into a block, and as bureaucratic if the highlighter warmth goes missing.

raised.raise: Status lives in line form (solid open, dashed pending, hatched taken, struck disabled), always with a word, never hue alone.
Choosing a block isolates it: its neighbours dim one step, so one item is held at a time.
Docs anatomy pins every label to its part on leader lines.
Everything snaps to one row module; new blocks arrive bright while settled ones recede.
Color owns whole blocks at full strength instead of being sprinkled as accents.

options.label: Campus Wayfinding
options.lineage: the CCS building's sign system: enamel room plates, floor directories, zone colors
options.thesis: The interface is the building's directory: plates, room codes and arrows route people to community, consultations and the restricted reports office.
options.viewport: A floor directory board fills the first screen: ACCS plate, three routed destinations with room codes, the reports office marked restricted.
options.risk: Familiar: Swiss-style wayfinding is where many runs in this category land, and oversized plates can turn institutional.

options.label: Sliding Rooms
options.lineage: the Rietveld Schröder house, fused with ACCS
options.thesis: One college workspace partitioned by sliding planes; the reports plane only slides open with permission.
options.viewport: Three planes compose the landing; sliding one reveals the next space, and the restricted plane shows its locked edge.
options.case: Carries the community-versus-reports boundary best, but CS students do not recognize De Stijl, so it loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Reads as an art-school homage if the planes do no real navigation work, and slide-heavy navigation can slow tasks.

options.label: Emission Rail
options.lineage: spectrogram plates on a viewing box
options.thesis: Every element registers to one rail; state is line height, dash and doubling.
options.viewport: A dark plate with destinations as ticks on one off-centre rail.
options.case: Students do not identify with spectrograms, and the rail hides community content.
options.kept: State carried by line form, not hue.
options.risk: Too dark and cold for a welcoming college space.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: One event held at a time; selecting a track dims the rest.
options.viewport: A ring section with tracks curling out from one collision.
options.case: A physics lab, not a college portal; WebGL tracks add nothing to posting or booking.
options.kept: Isolate on select: neighbours dim one step.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Layout follows a force network; labels pin to nodes on leader lines.
options.viewport: A force diagram of the college's spaces.
options.case: Engineering metaphor with no daily meaning for students or staff.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Numbered steps on a stud grid; new pieces arrive bright, prior ones ghost.
options.viewport: Step 1, 2, 3 spreads teaching how to use ACCS.
options.case: Recognizable but toy-like, which the brief rules out next to confidential reports.
options.kept: One row module; new arrives bright, settled recedes.

options.label: Lowbrow Panel
options.thesis: A packed, black-outlined tableau lacquered to a show finish.
options.viewport: A crowded tableau of outlined figures with a hand-lettered title.
options.case: Loud and playful, the opposite of a trustworthy college workspace.
options.kept: Color owns whole areas at full strength.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean edu-SaaS portal executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, two buttons and a product card stack; three feature columns below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other portal by design.
